panels.visual: A Greek fleet at Aulis with motionless ships on a flat calm sea, limp sails, soldiers sweating
panels.caption: The ships were stuck at Aulis with no wind at all. Agamemnon had angered Artemis.

panels.visual: A seer in a hooded cloak whispering to King Agamemnon who is turning pale, a flash of cold
panels.caption: A seer told him the wind would come only if he sacrificed his daughter Iphigenia.

panels.visual: King Agamemnon's face, torn between duty and grief, a tear running into his black beard, red cloak; behind him Iphigenia in a white veil with bowed head before an altar; no knife, no blood
panels.caption: No wind.

panels.visual: A white deer leaping through speed lines at the altar while a soft light carries Iphigenia away in the clouds, the sails of the ships filling with wind
panels.caption: In some versions, Artemis swapped her for a deer. The wind blew, and the ships sailed for Troy.
